newsitem.title: USA: U.S., two Koreas again try to arrange crucial meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S., two Koreas again try to arrange crucial meeting.

text.p: Representatives of the United States and the two Koreas held talks on Sunday to try again to arrange a twice-delayed meeting at which Pyongyang would announce if it would join in landmark peace talks.
The aim was to hold the meeting on Monday, but after several hours of discussion in New York a U.S. spokesman said there was no conclusion and the sides were still talking.

There were unconfirmed reports that senior negotiators from North Korea and South Korea were at the talks. But the U.S. spokesman said the American side was represented by a lower-level official, not chief negotiator Charles Kartman, who was reported to be in Washington.
"We are not having a heads-of-delegation meeting at which North Korea would respond to the U.S. and South Korean proposal" for four-party peace talks, the U.S. spokesman insisted.
"The United States is represented here only at the working level" in the person of Mark Minton, head of the State Department's Korea desk, he said.

The three delegations, headed by senior negotiators, first met last Wednesday to hear the North's formal response to a year-old U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-party peace talks that would finally close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing the fraying armistice with a peace treaty.

Although the discussions were inconclusive, negotiators reported "encouraging progress" and agreed to resume on Friday. However the North Koreans, saying they awaited instructions from Pyongyang, never showed for Friday's meeting, which was rescheduled for Saturday. The North Koreans again failed to appear on Saturday.
However, the three sides maintained "contacts" all weekend in hopes of getting the formal chief negotiators' meeting back on track.
Peace talks, if accepted by Pyongyang's Stalinist regime, might not begin until June or July. China would be the fourth participant along with the United States, South Korea and North Korea.
